Gates Cambridge is an international scholarship programme for outstanding postgraduate students at the University of Cambridge, set up in 2000 with a gift from the Gates Foundation.

opportunities.short_description: Fully funded joint master's degrees taught across two or more European universities. Open to students worldwide; most programmes take applications between October and January.

Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters are integrated master's programmes run by consortia of universities, usually with study periods in at least two countries. Master's-level students from anywhere in the world can apply, and many programmes offer full scholarships to top applicants.

Each programme runs its own admissions: most accept applications between October and January for courses starting the following autumn. Browse the official catalogue, pick programmes, and apply on each consortium's own website.

Not every programme still offers scholarships — some are at the end of their funding period — so check before you apply.

opportunities.short_description: $27,000 for a year of master's research at a Canadian university. Applications are due December 1 through the Research Portal.
opportunities.full_description:
The Canada Graduate Research Scholarship – Master's (which replaced the CGS M) gives $27,000 for 12 months to students starting or early in a master's or doctoral program at a Canadian institution with a CGRS M allocation.

You must be a Canadian citizen, permanent resident or protected person, have completed no more than 12 months of full-time study in the program by December 31, and usually have a first-class average in your last two years.

The deadline is December 1 at 8pm ET. Talk to your target school's graduate office early — some set internal deadlines before that.

The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships support postgraduate researchers in any discipline who have completed a master's degree, to carry out research or doctoral work at a Swiss university.

The scholarship pays CHF 2,450 a month. Applicants must be 35 or younger, come from one of 183 eligible countries, and have an academic supervisor in Switzerland who backs the application. You apply through the Swiss embassy in your country, and decisions are announced by the end of May.

Applications opened August 20, 2026; deadlines differ by country, so check your country's page. Applying is free.

You need to be in roughly the top 10% of your bachelor's programme, write your own pre-proposal for a master's thesis, and have two professors willing to send references. Interviews happen in February.

The application window for a 2027 start is November 1–30, 2026. Current or former ETH master's students and people who already hold a master's are not eligible.
